method: Reference-led procedural organ meshes. Botanical sources guide architecture and organ proportions; reference photographs are not redistributed as game textures.

plants.name: Rose
model_decisions: Seven irregular, tapered basal canes with outward lateral shoots retain an open shrub framework.
Five toothed leaflets share one pinnate rachis; small prickles occur on selected mature canes.
Twenty-eight flower sites have five green sepals and staggered, cupped petal whorls closing into a raised spiral heart.
Seedlings carry cotyledons and initial compound leaves; juvenile plants develop a smaller three-cane framework. Closed buds use mature flower attachments.

sources.title: RHS shrub roses
sources.evidence: Open spreading habit, arching prickly branches, and double flowers.

sources.title: RHS roses
sources.evidence: Glossy green leaves and cupped, rounded or rosette flower forms.

sources.title: RHS Rosa dumosa botanical details
sources.evidence: Rosa genus bears compound pinnate leaves; toothed leaflet margins inform the organ mesh.

sources.title: David Austin The Mayflower
sources.evidence: Breeder reference for pink double blooms held above dark foliage; the game model remains a generic shrub rose, not this named cultivar.

plants.name: Japanese maple
model_decisions: Tapered, gently sinuous trunk supports an irregular layered framework with fine opposite leafy shoots.
Each blade is one connected seven-lobed mesh with deep sinuses, shorter basal lobes and toothed margins.
Opposite paired leaves vary in angle, size and droop; open branch windows separate the canopy layers.
Seedling cotyledons precede true palmate leaves. Juvenile branching is authored separately, and the growth-bud display uses small unfurling leaf tips.

sources.title: NC State Extension Acer palmatum
sources.evidence: Palmate, deeply divided leaves with five to seven toothed lobes and varied small-tree forms.

sources.title: International Dendrology Society Acer palmatum
sources.evidence: Five to seven leaf lobes, divisions extending two-thirds to three-quarters toward the base, and double-serrate margins.

sources.title: RHS seven-lobed Japanese maple herbarium specimen
sources.evidence: RHS herbarium reference for a seven-lobed Acer palmatum form.

plants.name: Tropical hibiscus
model_decisions: Upright woody leaders carry broad, alternating, toothed leaves on actual petioles and secondary leafy twigs.
Twenty-four solitary flower sites preserve the existing catalogue's attachment count.
Each flower has five broad overlapping petals, a long staminal column, clustered anthers and five terminal stigma lobes.
Small leaf shoots and a compact branching juvenile precede pointed green buds at the mature flower attachments.

sources.title: RHS tropical hibiscus growing guide
sources.evidence: Woody tropical shrub with large showy flowers; the model retains the game's two-metre mature height.

sources.title: Singapore NParks Hibiscus rosa-sinensis Hi Fever
sources.evidence: Woody shrub, toothed petiolate leaves and solitary five-petalled trumpet flowers; anatomy informs the generic coral form.

sources.title: NC State Extension Hibiscus rosa-sinensis
sources.evidence: Existing catalogue species reference retained for botanical identity and flower anatomy.

plants.name: Hardy fuchsia
model_decisions: Arching fine canes support paired, finely toothed leaves and lateral leafy twigs, retaining spaces through the crown.
Ninety-six pendent flowers hang clear of mature foliage from outer leaf axils and fine descending terminal pedicels.
Every flower has a bent pedicel, ovary, scarlet calyx tube, four reflexed sepals, four shorter purple petals and eight projecting stamens.
Flower size respects the game's existing attachment envelope. Closed elongated buds reuse precisely the same flower sites; early stages have independently authored shoot structures.

sources.title: RHS Fuchsia magellanica
sources.evidence: Scarlet sepals with purple corolla, opposite or whorled leaves, tubular calyx, four spreading sepals and four erect petals.

sources.title: Oxford University Plants 400 Fuchsia magellanica
sources.evidence: Upright semi-climbing shrub with pendent crimson flowers and violet-purple inner petals.

sources.title: Oregon State University Fuchsia magellanica photographs
sources.evidence: Reference photographs and botanical description of red-brown stems, opposite leaves and pendent flowers.

sources.title: RHS Fuchsia magellanica var. gracilis reference photograph
sources.evidence: Visible relationship between arching slender branches, leaf pairs and hanging crimson-and-purple flowers.
